newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Harmonised CPI lowers Portugal's key avge rate - INE.
newsitem.headline: Harmonised CPI lowers Portugal's key avge rate - INE.

text.p: Harmonised inflation data issued by Eurostat, the European Union's statistics body, would put Portugal's rolling 12-month average inflation at three percent in January, down from the National Statistics Institute's (INE) figure of 3.2 percent, INE said.
The rolling average figure is the government's benchmark.
Eurostat issued on Friday for the first time harmonised inflation figures for the 15 European Union member states.
According to these figures, Portugal's January month-on-month inflation was 0.4 percent, with the year-on-year rate at 2.8 percent and the 12-month rolling average at 3.0 percent.
Those compare with INE's January figures of 0.3 percent, 3.3 percent and 3.2 percent, respectively.
According to INE chief economist Daniel Santos, the main differences between the national price index and the harmonised version was the exclusion from the latter of some health and education items.
